value.rationale: A bidirectional, parameter-robust counterexample on strongly convex, scalar, two-component problems disproves any blanket stability dominance of random reshuffling over iid sampling (or vice versa) for standard SAGA. Equal components show the phenomenon is not driven by gradient curvature heterogeneity. It is a meaningful algorithmic sampling-design boundary rather than a recomputation of a known table.
